story.title: Eiffel Tower Reopens After Staff Walkout Over Hindu Group's Request to Limit Women
story.summary: The Eiffel Tower reopened on Tuesday following a staff walkout in protest of management instructions that limited the presence of women during a visit by a Hindu religious group. The Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) later apologized for any inconvenience caused. The operating company acknowledged that the conditions requested by the delegation should not have been accepted.

key_facts: Eiffel Tower staff walked out over the removal of women colleagues during a Hindu group's visit.
The Hindu group involved is the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS).
The Eiffel Tower reopened on September 6, 2026, after the protest.
The operating company admitted that the request to limit interactions with women should not have been accepted.

related_stories.title: Trump Issues Threat Against Bombardier's US Sales Amid Trade Tensions
related_stories.summary: Donald Trump has threatened to prevent Canadian aircraft manufacturer Bombardier from selling its planes in the United States unless the company relocates its manufacturing operations to the US. This warning comes as trade tensions escalate between the two countries, particularly in light of Canada's tariffs on US imports, which can reach up to 50%. Previously, Trump had also expressed intentions to decertify Bombardier aircraft due to certification disputes regarding US-made planes.
